name: Droost
description: Developer-acceleration toolkit for AI coding agents working on Drupal: exposes application/codebase introspection plus tiered, gated write/exec tools over MCP (Model Context Protocol). A Drupal analog of Laravel Boost. LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY (install with require-dev); not for production.
project_description: Droost is a local-development toolkit that lets an AI coding agent ask a Drupal site about itself and then build on it deterministically. It is the Drupal analog of Laravel Boost. Agents writing Drupal code normally work blind: they do not know which modules and versions are installed, what entity types and fields exist, which service to type-hint instead of calling \Drupal::, or whether the last request errored. Droost exposes that information as schema-described MCP tools returning structured JSON, and adds tiered, individually gated write, database, entity, configuration, scaffold and code-evaluation tools. It is built entirely on the MCP Server module (drupal/mcp_server), which supplies the MCP runtime and the #[Tool] plugin system; Droost supplies the tools. The base module ships the read-only introspection tools plus the gated write/exec surface (config set, raw SQL create/update/delete, entity CRUD, module install/uninstall, cron, cache rebuild, scaffold, structure create, and PHP eval); a family of submodules add semantic/code-graph search, an AI-provider bridge, devel_generate content, Drupal Canvas support, Views composition, a codebase wiki, and more. Every state-changing tool is disabled by default and only acts when the operator opts in through per-category droost.settings flags, and the most dangerous tools additionally refuse to run over anything but the local CLI/STDIO transport. The gates reduce footguns; the module states plainly that they are not a security boundary against an untrusted caller. Install it with require-dev and enable it only on local and trusted development environments; never on a production or internet-reachable site. This documents the 1.0.0-rc1 pre-release.
